Research problem: Can MVFA's few-shot inference be made inductive, scoring each image only with statistics of the K normal support images and source-validation data instead of test-set min-max normalisation, while keeping image AUROC within 1 point of the re-run transductive baseline and making each image's score invariant to the composition of the rest of the test set (prevalence 10-50%, with and without outliers)? The replacement is evaluated component by component (normalisation, then fusion weight, then image-level aggregation), with sensitivity at 95% specificity and expected calibration error reported alongside AUROC.
Target paper title: Adapting Visual-Language Models for Generalizable Anomaly Detection in Medical Images
Target paper abstract: Recent advancements in large-scale visual-language pre-trained models have led to significant progress in zero-/few-shot anomaly detection within natural image domains. However, the substantial domain divergence between natural and medical images limits the effectiveness of these methodologies in medical anomaly detection. This paper introduces a novel lightweight multi-level adaptation and comparison framework to repurpose the CLIP model for medical anomaly detection. Our approach integrates multiple residual adapters into the pre-trained visual encoder, enabling a stepwise enhancement of visual features across different levels. This multi-level adaptation is guided by multi-level, pixel-wise visual-language feature alignment loss functions, which recalibrate the model's focus from object semantics in natural imagery to anomaly identification in medical images. The adapted features exhibit improved generalization across various medical data types, even in zero-shot scenarios where the model encounters unseen medical modalities and anatomical regions during training. Our experiments on medical anomaly detection benchmarks demonstrate that our method significantly surpasses current state-of-the-art models, with an average AUC improvement of 6.24% and 7.33% for anomaly classification, 2.03% and 2.37% for anomaly segmentation, under the zero-shot and few-shot settings, respectively. Source code is available at: https://github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD
Verified facts about the target paper's code: Code-verified facts about the public code of the source paper (github.com/MediaBrain-SJTU/MVFA-AD):
- CLIP/adapter.py: CLIP_Inplanted wraps a frozen CLIP ViT-L/14-336 (input 240x240); ClipAdapter bottleneck adapters are inserted after layers [6, 12, 18, 24]; there are two adapter sets, seg_adapters (segmentation branch) and det_adapters (detection branch), mixed residually with ratio 0.1.
- prompt.py / utils.py: the text side is two frozen text anchors (normal, abnormal) averaged over 35 templates.
- train_zero.py (zero-shot, leave-one-dataset-out): det branch trained with BCE on the MEAN-pooled patch anomaly map for every image; seg branch trained with Focal + Dice on pixel masks only for BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC; batch size 1; the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- train_few.py: few-shot fine-tuning on K normal + K abnormal (masked) images from BMAD's valid/ split, one fixed draw (dataset/fewshot_seed); the checkpoint is selected on the target test set.
- test_few.py: zero-shot map (text similarity) and few-shot map (1 - max cosine to a memory bank of support patch features, per level) are each min-max normalised over the whole test set and added with weight 0.5; image score = max of fused pixel map (masked datasets) or mean-pooled det score (others).
- BMAD: BrainMRI, LiverCT, RESC have masks; OCT17, ChestXray, HIS have image labels only; each has train/valid/test splits.

The research idea:
TITLE: Leave-one-out empirical-CDF normalisation for inductive per-image MVFA scoring
SUMMARY: Replace test-set min-max normalisation with each branch's leave-one-out empirical CDF over support-normal patch scores, fuse in CDF space, and pool with a top-k mean.
HYPOTHESIS: On held-out BMAD modalities with K >= 4, LOO empirical-CDF scoring keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, while each image's score is exactly invariant to test-set resampling (shift 0 vs. a median shift above 0.05 for the transductive pipeline) and the support-derived threshold gives realised specificity within 5 points of 95%.
RESEARCH IDEA: Independent variable: normalisation of the zero-shot and few-shot branches (test-set min-max vs. support LOO empirical CDF vs. support z-score). For level l and branch b, the reference set R_bl contains the patch scores of each support normal computed against a memory bank built from the other K-1 supports (few-shot) or against the text anchors (zero-shot). A test patch score s is mapped to F_bl(s) = (rank of s in R_bl + 0.5)/(|R_bl| + 1). The fused patch score is the mean of F over branches and levels. Image score = mean of the top 1% fused patches. Dependent variables: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity with the threshold set at the 95th percentile of support LOO image scores, realised specificity, ECE, and the per-image score shift under test-set resampling.
RATIONALE: MVFA's few-shot scores come from 1 - max cosine to a support memory bank and from text similarity, two scales that the code reconciles with test-set min-max. ReCAP's non-parametric normal memory suggests calibrating each branch against the empirical distribution of normal scores obtained from the supports themselves. A leave-one-out empirical CDF maps every branch and level to the same [0, 1] scale defined only by the K supports, so each test image can be scored alone and the fused score has a fixed meaning (fraction of normal patches that are less anomalous).
METHOD: 1) test_few.py: refactor into score_image(x, model, support_feats, refs) that uses no other test image. 2) utils.py: build_refs(support_feats, text_feats): for i in 1..K, memory bank from supports except i; compute few-shot patch scores of support i per level (1 - max cosine) and zero-shot scores (softmax over normal/abnormal anchors, as in MVFA); store sorted arrays R_bl. 3) cdf(s, R) via torch.searchsorted. 4) Fused map = mean over b, l of cdf maps (upsampled as in MVFA). 5) Image score = mean of top 1% pixels; threshold tau = 95th percentile of LOO image scores of the supports. 6) Remove the min-max block (test_few.py lines 220-241). Hyper-parameters: top 1%, nominal specificity 95%; no training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA checkpoints retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2,4,8,16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws, mean and std. Baselines: the original transductive pipeline (test-set min-max, 0.5, max pooling) and a plain support z-score. Ordered ablation: (i) normalisation only (keep 0.5 weights and max pooling), (ii) + CDF-space fusion, (iii) + top-1% pooling. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity, realised specificity, ECE (logistic map fitted on source validation), per-image score shift when 50% of the test set is resampled at 10%, 30% and 50% prevalence. Falsified if image AUROC drops by more than 1 point at K >= 4 or realised specificity misses 95% by more than 5 points.
